Wow, this is insane. Hopefully this will be available for the public to play around with even if it is in early development.

I believe it is, but you don't want to try to run it on your personal computer. Most of what I submit has code available, if you dig around. However, you want stuff like 1024 cores and a few TB of RAM.

I used to model traffic, but I don't have anything like that at home. I've been thinking about spinning up some on-demand stuff at AWS and seeing what fun I can have, but my time is pretty occupied.

That's basically been my barrier into a lot of this stuff, I got a 3 GIG graphics card, 16 gigs of ram, and a high end processor but I'm half tempted to upgrade with a lot of stuff that is coming out now, problem is some of the components like graphics cards are way up right now, going to have to wait till there is a bit of a calm in the market. Hopefully things like this will push the need/want for innovation in making major leaps in terms of hardware for the end consumer. I know there are components out there that would do the job but I'm not a millionaire by any stretch of the imagination.

Yeah, I've a tower with 32 GB and a server to run my home network and it has 64 GB. I wouldn't even think about trying to run this sort of stuff on those. I mostly just use the RAM to be able to spin up VMs. I don't have a good reason, I just like playing with VMs.

When I sold my company, I signed a non-compete, so I can't really model traffic or work in that field anymore. So, I use this compute power to spin up various distros and oddball operating systems. It's still not enough compute power to run anything interesting in the AI field.

It's funny, really. I touched my first computer in about 1971. Back then, I couldn't even dream of computers this powerful. Now we have them and they still aren't powerful enough. I have a laptop with 32 GB of RAM... It still bogs down on some videos. WTF?

I think it's an industry still going through a lot of growing pains. I think every time there have been things on the cutting edge in a technological sense, both during and before my time the people trying to push out the stuff that was considered far future stuff like graphical interfaces were a pipe dream and on in house systems were barely functional and would crash all the time due to hardware limitations. I think it's one of those areas where we have to make things more efficient, in the same way different video and audio codecs have become more efficient and allow us to store something for much less data, and in the same way specific machines are now being built for crypto-currency mining, I think there will probably be an AI hardware software specialized industry that can specialize builds that are made specifically for doing the tasks at hand and are more efficient at doing them then what is being built now. Even home computers are still in their infancy compared to other fields we're still innovating in that have been around for centuries.

I guess we just have to hope we don't end up blowing each other up before it happens. Some days I'm an optimist and other days I just think "good lord how can people still be there" not even with specific thoughts (although of course that's a byproduct) just the type of thinking in general is broken.

That's part of my incentive to learn, personal responsibility. I can't learn or do everything, but I've never been complacent and I frown on people that are that way when it comes to anything. That's my little rant for the day.
